source_name: 35/2017. (XII. 14.) MNB rendelet a pénzforgalom lebonyolításáról (Payment Execution Decree)
why_relevant: The operational rulebook for executing payments in Hungary — instant payment (azonnali átutalás) rules, execution deadlines, value limits, request-to-pay, secondary account identifiers. It is amended frequently (e.g. 57/2022. (XII. 22.), 41/2024. (VIII. 29.)) and each amendment carries hard implementation dates that banks and PSPs must build to. Highest-value single decree in the cell for payments compliance dates.

source_name: Mnbtv. — 2013. évi CXXXIX. törvény a Magyar Nemzeti Bankról (MNB Act)
why_relevant: Defines the MNB's rule-making and supervisory powers, including the legal basis and procedural limits for MNB rendeletek and supervisory sanctions. Needed to interpret which supervisory instruments are legally binding versus soft guidance — a recurring classification problem for a compliance calendar.

source_name: MNB rendeletek index (mnb.hu central bank decrees listing)
why_relevant: The issuer's own chronological index of every MNB rendelet, including reporting-obligation decrees (adatszolgáltatási MNB rendeletek) and payment decrees. Faster and better-structured than gazette scraping for detecting a new MNB rendelet, and it links straight to the binding text. Pointer because it indexes rather than promulgates.

source_name: MNB Pénzforgalom — Szabályozás (payments regulation hub)
why_relevant: The MNB's payments-domain regulatory landing page, bundling the payment decrees, the Pft., and the relevant EU acts in one place with issuer commentary. Useful for confirming which instruments govern a given payment obligation and for catching announcements of forthcoming decree amendments.

source_name: Wolters Kluwer net.jogtar.hu — Hatályos Jogszabályok Gyűjteménye (free tier)
why_relevant: The commercially-maintained free consolidated database of Hungarian law in force, with the most stable and widely-cited deep-link scheme (docid=a1300237.tv). Valuable as a cross-check against NJT: divergence between the two consolidations is itself a signal of a recent or contested amendment. Free tier gives text in force plus the next upcoming időállapot.

source_name: mkogy.jogtar.hu — Törvények és országgyűlési határozatok (Parliament-facing statute database)
why_relevant: Parliament's Jogtár-powered collection of acts and parliamentary resolutions, including historical acts (e.g. the superseded 1996. évi CXII. Hpt.) and newly adopted amendment acts such as 2025. évi C. törvény a pénzügyi közvetítőrendszert érintő törvények módosításáról. Useful for lineage tracing — what an obligation looked like before an amendment.

source_name: Országgyűlés — Folyamatban lévő törvényjavaslatok / Irományok (bills in progress)
why_relevant: Bills (T/xxxxx irományok) are visible here weeks before promulgation in Magyar Közlöny, giving the earliest hard signal of a coming statutory deadline. Financial-sector omnibus bills — e.g. 2025. évi C. törvény on amendments to acts affecting the financial intermediary system, and the 2026 financial-sector harmonisation bills — pass through this pipeline together with committee (TAB) amendment papers.

source_name: A Kormány törvényalkotási programja (Government semi-annual legislative programme)
why_relevant: The forward-looking government plan listing which bills will be submitted in a given session (spring/autumn), with intended submission months. This is the earliest structured, official forward calendar available — months ahead of gazette publication — and it names financial-sector and EU-harmonisation items explicitly.

source_name: Kormany.hu Dokumentumtár — jogszabálytervezetek társadalmi egyeztetése (ministry draft-decree consultations)
why_relevant: Government and ministerial decree drafts affecting banks and PSPs are posted here for társadalmi egyeztetés with a stated comment deadline and a ministry mailbox (historically tarsadalmiegyeztetes@pm.gov.hu for the finance ministry). Gives both the draft binding text and a concrete consultation deadline — directly on-topic for the 'consultations' and 'deadlines' topics of this run.

source_name: egyeztetes.kormany.hu — Társadalmi egyeztetések, párbeszédek portal
why_relevant: Dedicated government consultation portal, structurally separate from the Dokumentumtár. Needs to be monitored alongside it because draft instruments are not consistently posted to both; missing one is a realistic way to miss a comment deadline.

source_name: jog.gov.hu — Magyar Jogi Információs Portál (Aktuális Magyar Közlönyök)
why_relevant: State-run legal information portal that aggregates current gazette issues alongside NJT (njt.jog.gov.hu is on the same domain family). Serves as a lightweight, structured entry point to the day's gazette content and a redundancy path if magyarkozlony.hu is unavailable.

source_name: Jogászvilág — Jogszabályfigyelő (weekly gazette digest)
why_relevant: Wolters Kluwer's professional weekly digest of what appeared in Magyar Közlöny, week by week, in plain Hungarian legal prose. Excellent triage layer: it flags financial-sector harmonisation amendments quickly and provides human-readable context, reducing false negatives from keyword-only gazette scraping. Not authoritative — always resolve back to the gazette text.

source_name: torvenyfigyelo.hu — Folyamatban lévő törvényjavaslatok tracker
why_relevant: Independent aggregator that re-presents pending Hungarian bills in a simpler, more scrapeable structure than parlament.hu. Useful as a redundancy/cross-check on the bill pipeline; provenance and maintenance cadence unverified, so it should never be the sole basis for a deadline.

source_name: KávéKözlöny — plain-language summaries of each Magyar Közlöny issue
why_relevant: Issue-by-issue AI-generated plain-Hungarian summaries of the official gazette, useful purely as a fast triage signal to decide which issues merit full parsing. The site itself states the official text on magyarkozlony.hu remains authoritative; treat as untrusted for any date or obligation.

source_name: EUR-Lex National Implementing Measures (NIM/MNE) — Hungary
why_relevant: The EU-side register of which Hungarian statutes Member State authorities have formally notified as transposing a given directive, updated weekly. It is the bridge that connects an EU deadline (e.g. CCD2, PSD3 once adopted) to the specific Hungarian act number — the exact join a transposition-deadline calendar needs, and it also reveals when Hungary has NOT yet notified.

source_name: N-Lex — EU gateway to the Hungarian national law database
why_relevant: Commission-run gateway describing and querying Hungary's national legislative database through a harmonised interface. Chiefly valuable as documentation of the Hungarian database's structure and query semantics, which helps design a robust NJT crawler, and as an alternative query path.

source_name: Magyar Közlöny Lap- és Könyvkiadó / MKIFK — publisher and webshop
why_relevant: The publisher operating both magyarkozlony.hu and (via MKIFK Magyar Közlönykiadó és Igazságügyi Fordítóközpont Zrt.) the Nemzeti Jogszabálytár. Relevant for establishing provenance, authenticity (digital signature scheme), licensing terms for reuse, and for purchasing/archival access to back issues via webshop.mhk.hu.

source_name: Arcanum Digitheca — Magyar Közlöny archive 1945–2019
why_relevant: Full-text searchable historical archive of the gazette back to 1945. Not needed for forward-looking compliance dates, but essential when reconstructing the history of a long-lived obligation (e.g. tracing an Hpt. provision back through the 1996. évi CXII. regime) or dating a repealed requirement.

source_name: Tietoevry Banking — Press Releases / Newsroom
why_relevant: Nordic card/payments vendor that publicly announced completing OTP Bank Hungary's card acquiring software replacement, explicitly citing card-scheme and EU/national regulatory compliance as drivers. Vendor newsroom is the only public trace of a privately-owned Hungarian bank's payments procurement.

source_name: Google Cloud Customers — OTP Bank case study
why_relevant: Hyperscaler customer-reference page in which OTP Bank names MNB (Magyar Nemzeti Bank) requirements as a main driver for adopting Apigee API gateway — a textbook indirect trace of a compliance-driven buying decision at a private bank.

source_name: Thought Machine — Press Releases / Newsroom
why_relevant: Announced Magyar Bankholding (now MBH Bank) selecting Vault Core for a digital-first bank — the single largest core-banking purchasing decision in Hungary of recent years, publicly visible only because the vendor announced it.

source_name: Dorsum — News / case studies (Hungarian wealth & securities software vendor)
why_relevant: Hungarian-headquartered banking software vendor publishing detailed accounts of its joint IT implementation and migration project with Magyar Bankholding/MBH — names the bank, the systems and the migration timetable.

source_name: MINDSPIRE — Banki és biztosítói transzformációs szolgáltatások (blog + service pages)
why_relevant: Hungarian banking-transformation consultancy that publishes Hungarian-language blog posts on core-banking selection, naming platforms (Flexcube, T24, Murex, CAMS) and describing real domestic selection failures. Reveals which core systems are actually shortlisted by Hungarian banks and what compliance constraints shape the RFP.

source_name: Integra Zrt. — PR / referenciák (Hungarian banking software house)
why_relevant: Long-established Hungarian vendor of software for domestic banks, brokerages and Hungarian branches of foreign banks; its PR/reference page is one of the few Hungarian-language listings of named bank clients and delivered modules.

source_name: 4iG Nyrt. — corporate site / news (Hungary's leading systems integrator)
why_relevant: Largest Hungarian SI, explicitly advertising 'full support of banking data reporting' (banki adatszolgáltatás) among its services. As a listed company it also files regulatory announcements that occasionally reveal financial-sector contract wins not otherwise public.

source_name: Portfolio Financial IT / Banking Technology conference — programme, speakers and sponsor pages
why_relevant: The single best pointer source for the Hungarian bank-IT supplier landscape: annual conference whose 'támogatók' (sponsors) and 'előadók' (speakers) pages enumerate essentially every vendor selling into Hungarian banks, and whose agendas name the regulatory topics (DORA, AFR/qvik, PSD3) driving spend.

source_name: ITBUSINESS.hu — Hungarian IT trade press, finance vertical
why_relevant: Hungarian IT trade magazine that runs vendor-sourced articles on banking IT projects (data warehouse, cloud core banking, DORA readiness) and its own 'Finance & Technology' event. Frequently the first Hungarian-language publication of a vendor-bank engagement, and explicitly links projects to regulation (e.g. DORA article).
